{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_7fde5192e4e4433080db8fef","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Tmux Detector Poller — Design Document\n2\t\n3\t## Overview\n4\t\n5\tThe tmux detector is a **harness-agnostic fallback** for detecting stuck Claude Code sessions (or any coding harness) without relying on hook events. It watches opted-in tmux panes and emits stuck/unstuck events to the daemon's `/event/normalized` endpoint.\n6\t\n7\tThis design answers the key architectural questions and provides an implementable specification.\n8\t\n9\t---\n10\t\n11\t## Design Goals\n12\t\n13\t1. **Harness-agnostic detection** — Works for any coding harness, not just Claude Code\n14\t2. **Opt-in model** — Panes explicitly opt-in; no surprise monitoring\n15\t3. **Low false-positive rate** — Avoid flagging active sessions as stuck\n16\t4. **Self-contained operation** — No harness hooks required\n17\t5. **Graceful degradation** — Handles panes that close, disappear, or change state\n18\t\n19\t---\n20\t\n21\t## Key Design Decisions\n22\t\n23\t### 1. Opt-In Mechanism\n24\t\n25\t**Decision: Pane-title prefix pattern**\n26\t\n27\tPanes opt-in by including a specific prefix in their title. The detector polls all panes and filters for those with the matching prefix.\n28\t\n29\t**Why not alternatives:**\n30\t\n31\t| Alternative | Rejected Because |\n32\t|-------------|------------------|\n33\t| tmux user option (`@trailboss-monitor`) | Requires pane-specific configuration per session; not discoverable via `list-panes`; doesn't persist across pane reuse |\n34\t| Manual pane ID registration | Requires user to know pane IDs upfront; doesn't handle dynamic pane creation |\n35\t| Environment variable in pane | Not discoverable from outside the pane; requires harness cooperation |\n36\t| Session name pattern | Too coarse; affects all panes in a session |\n37\t\n38\t**Chosen approach:**\n39\t\n40\t- **Prefix:** `@tb-` (trail-boss)\n41\t- **Detection:** `tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_title}' | grep '@tb-'`\n42\t- **Example pane title:** `@tb-alpha: implementing feature X`\n43\t- **User sets it via:** `tmux rename-window '@tb-alpha: working on task'` or shell that sets the title\n44\t\n45\t**Advantages:**\n46\t- Visible to the user (they can see which panes are monitored)\n47\t- Discoverable via standard tmux commands\n48\t- Works across sessions and windows\n49\t- No per-pane configuration files\n50\t- Harness-agnostic (just a title string)\n51\t\n52\t**Opt-out mechanism:** User removes the prefix from the title; detector automatically stops tracking.\n53\t\n54\t---\n55\t\n56\t### 2. Detecting \"Quiet\"\n57\t\n58\t**Decision: `capture-pane` output hash comparison**\n59\t\n60\tThe detector captures the visible output of each opted-in pane on each poll cycle and computes a hash of the content. If the hash hasn't changed across polls and the quiet threshold has elapsed, the pane is considered \"quiet.\"\n61\t\n62\t**Why this approach:**\n63\t\n64\t- **Reliable:** `tmux capture-pane -p -t <pane>` returns the exact visible content\n65\t- **No harness cooperation needed:** Works for any process running in the pane\n66\t- **Portable:** Standard tmux command, available on all systems\n67\t- **Deterministic:** Same content → same hash\n68\t\n69\t**Hash algorithm (simplified for speed):**\n70\t\n71\t```\n72\thash = concat(\n73\t  first_line_length,\n74\t  last_line_length,\n75\t  first_10_chars_of_first_line,\n76\t  last_10_chars_of_last_line,\n77\t  total_line_count\n78\t)\n79\t```\n80\t\n81\tThis avoids storing full pane contents while detecting changes with high confidence. False positives are unlikely in practice (different content producing identical hash values).\n82\t\n83\t**Poll interval:** 2 seconds (configurable)\n84\t\n85\t- Tradeoff: Lower interval = faster detection but more CPU usage\n86\t- 2 seconds catches stuck sessions within a few seconds of occurrence\n87\t- tmux `capture-pane` is lightweight; overhead is acceptable\n88\t\n89\t---\n90\t\n91\t### 3. Prompt-Like Last Line Detection\n92\t\n93\t**Decision: Regex pattern matching on last non-empty line**\n94\t\n95\tBefore declaring a pane \"stuck,\" the detector checks whether the last line looks like a prompt. This reduces false positives (e.g., a long-running command with no output yet).\n96\t\n97\t**Prompt patterns (configurable):**\n98\t\n99\t```javascript\n100\tconst PROMPT_PATTERNS = [\n101\t  /\\$\\s*$/,           // bash/zsh $\n102\t  />\\s*$/,            // many shells >\n103\t  /#\\s*$/,            // root #\n104\t  /\\?\\s*$/,           // confirmation prompts\n105\t  /\\[.*?\\]\\s*$/,      // bracketed prompts like [y/N]\n106\t  /:\\s*$/,            // colon prompts\n107\t  />>>\\s*$/,          // Python REPL\n108\t  /\\.\\.\\.\\s*$/,       // Python continuation\n109\t  />\\s*\\>/,           // MySQL prompt\n110\t  /@/,                // Augie/other shells\n111\t];\n112\t```\n113\t\n114\t**Algorithm:**\n115\t\n116\t```\n117\t1. Capture pane output\n118\t2. Split by newlines\n119\t3. Find last non-empty line\n120\t4. Trim whitespace\n121\t5. Match against PROMPT_PATTERNS\n122\t6. If any pattern matches → \"looks like prompt\" → can be stuck\n123\t7. If no pattern matches → not stuck (might be mid-computation)\n124\t```\n125\t\n126\t**False-positive mitigation:**\n127\t\n128\t- A pane that's quiet but whose last line doesn't match any prompt pattern is **not** considered stuck\n129\t- Example: A long-running `make` with no output yet → last line might be the command itself, not a prompt → not stuck\n130\t- Once actual output appears, the prompt detection will re-evaluate on the next quiet period\n131\t\n132\t**Extensibility:**\n133\t\n134\t- Patterns are configurable via environment variable or config file\n135\t- Users can add harness-specific patterns (e.g., Augie's `@` prompt)\n136\t- Future enhancement: Learn prompts from pane history\n137\t\n138\t---\n139\t\n140\t### 4. Quiet Threshold\n141\t\n142\t**Decision: 30 seconds (configurable)**\n143\t\n144\tA pane must be quiet for 30 seconds before being considered \"stuck.\"\n145\t\n146\t**Why 30 seconds:**\n147\t\n148\t- **Not too short:** Avoids flagging momentary pauses (e.g., agent thinking, network latency)\n149\t- **Not too long:** Catches stuck sessions within a reasonable time\n150\t- **Human scale:** 30 seconds is perceptible but not annoying\n151\t- **Empirical:** Claude Code turns often complete within seconds; 30s suggests a genuine block\n152\t\n153\t**Tradeoffs:**\n154\t\n155\t| Threshold | Pros | Cons |\n156\t|-----------|------|------|\n157\t| 10s | Faster detection | More false positives (thinking periods) |\n158\t| 30s (chosen) | Balanced | Slower to catch very short blocks |\n159\t| 60s | Fewer false positives | Slower detection; user may notice first |\n160\t\n161\t**Configurability:**\n162\t\n163\t- Environment variable: `TRAILBOSS_QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS` (default: 30000)\n164\t- CLI flag: `--quiet-threshold <ms>` (for detector script)\n165\t- Config file: `~/.config/trail-boss/config.toml` (future)\n166\t\n167\t---\n168\t\n169\t### 5. Unstuck Detection\n170\t\n171\t**Decision: Any output change = unstuck**\n172\t\n173\tWhen a pane is marked as stuck, the detector continues polling. On the next poll cycle:\n174\t\n175\t1. Capture pane output\n176\t2. Compute hash\n177\t3. Compare to last-known hash\n178\t4. If hash changed → emit `unstuck` event → clear stuck state\n179\t\n180\t**Why this is correct:**\n181\t\n182\t- **Universal:** Any new output means the session is no longer blocked\n183\t- **Prompt-agnostic:** Works for any harness, any prompt style\n184\t- **Covers all cases:**\n185\t  - User typed input → new output → unstuck\n186\t  - Agent resumed (e.g., after auto-retry) → new output → unstuck\n187\t  - Command finished → new prompt → unstuck\n188\t\n189\t**Edge cases handled:**\n190\t\n191\t- **Pane closed:** Detected via `pane_exists()` check → emit `ended` event\n192\t- **Pane reused by new session:** Detected via title change (if title doesn't match `@tb-` prefix) → automatically untracked\n193\t- **Transient output (e.g., blinking cursor):** Hash comparison ignores whitespace-only changes\n194\t\n195\t---\n196\t\n197\t### 6. Session ID Generation\n198\t\n199\t**Decision: Synthetic session ID from pane ID + timestamp**\n200\t\n201\tFor the tmux detector, there is no harness-provided session ID. The detector generates a **synthetic session ID** that uniquely identifies a pane monitoring session.\n202\t\n203\t**Format:** `tmux-{paneId}-{startTimestamp}`\n204\t\n205\t**Example:** `tmux-%446-1719987600000`\n206\t\n207\t**Why this format:**\n208\t\n209\t- **Pane ID:** Ties the synthetic session to a specific tmux pane (`%446`)\n210\t- **Start timestamp:** Makes the ID unique across restarts (same pane reused later = different ID)\n211\t- **Prefix `tmux-`:** Clearly indicates this is a synthetic session from the detector\n212\t\n213\t**Stability:**\n214\t\n215\t- The synthetic ID is generated when the detector first starts tracking a pane\n216\t- It persists until:\n217\t  - The pane is closed (`ended` event)\n218\t  - The pane title no longer matches `@tb-` (automatic untrack)\n219\t  - The detector restarts (new synthetic IDs for all panes)\n220\t\n221\t**Bootstrap entries in daemon:**\n222\t\n223\tWhen a pane is first detected as stuck, the daemon receives a `stuck` event with a synthetic `sessionId`. The daemon treats this as a **bootstrap entry** — a session that exists only for queue purposes, with no transcript or reconcile loop.\n224\t\n225\t**Limitations:**\n226\t\n227\t- **No transcript path:** Synthetic sessions have no `transcript.jsonl` to reconcile\n228\t- **No `cwd` auto-discovery:** Must use `pane_current_path` (tmux built-in)\n229\t- **No harness-specific context:** Can't distinguish `permission` vs `stopped` — always uses `reason: \"stopped\"`\n230\t- **Fragile across restarts:** Detector restart → new synthetic IDs → old entries orphaned (daemon will age them out)\n231\t\n232\tThese limitations are acceptable for a **fallback detector** — the primary Claude Code adapter (hooks) provides full fidelity.\n233\t\n234\t---\n235\t\n236\t## State Machine\n237\t\n238\tPer-pane state machine:\n239\t\n240\t```\n241\t                    ┌─────────────────┐\n242\t                    │   UNTRACKED     │  ← Pane doesn't exist or title lacks @tb- prefix\n243\t                    └────────┬────────┘\n244\t                             │ pane appears with @tb- title\n245\t                             ▼\n246\t                    ┌─────────────────┐\n247\t                    │   REGISTERED    │  ← Initial registration, emit 'registered' event\n248\t                    └────────┬────────┘\n249\t                             │\n250\t                             │ poll loop\n251\t                             ▼\n252\t                    ┌─────────────────┐\n253\t          ┌────────▶│   MONITORING    │ ◀─────┐  ← Normal polling state\n254\t          │         └────────┬────────┘      │\n255\t          │                  │               │\n256\t          │                  │ output        │ quiet for >30s\n257\t          │                  │ changed       │ AND last line looks\n258\t          │                  │               │ like prompt\n259\t          │                  │               │\n260\t          │    ┌─────────────┴───────────────┴────────────┐\n261\t          │    │                                       │\n262\t          │    │ (was stuck)                          │ (was not stuck)\n263\t          │    ▼                                       ▼\n264\t          │ ┌─────────┐                         ┌─────────────┐\n265\t          │ │ UNSTUCK │                         │    STUCK    │  ← Emit 'stuck' event\n266\t          │ └────┬────┘                         └──────┬──────┘\n267\t          │      │                                     │\n268\t          │      │ emit 'unstuck' event                │\n269\t          │      └─────────────┬───────────────────────┘\n270\t          │                    │\n271\t          └────────────────────┘\n272\t                                │\n273\t                                │ pane closed or title loses @tb-\n274\t                                ▼\n275\t                         ┌─────────────────┐\n276\t                         │  UNTRACKING     │  ← Emit 'ended' event\n277\t                         └─────────────────┘\n278\t```\n279\t\n280\t**States:**\n281\t\n282\t- **UNTRACKED:** Not monitoring (pane doesn't exist or title lacks prefix)\n283\t- **REGISTERED:** Initial registration (emits `registered` event, transitions to MONITORING)\n284\t- **MONITORING:** Normal polling (checking for output changes)\n285\t- **STUCK:** Quiet for >30s at a prompt (emitted `stuck` event, awaiting output change)\n286\t- **UNSTUCK:** Output changed after being stuck (emits `unstuck` event, returns to MONITORING)\n287\t- **UNTRACKING:** Pane closed or prefix removed (emits `ended` event, removes from tracking)\n288\t\n289\t---\n290\t\n291\t## Poll Loop Pseudocode\n292\t\n293\t```javascript\n294\t// Configuration\n295\tconst POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 2000;           // Check every 2 seconds\n296\tconst QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS = 30000;         // 30 seconds of quiet = stuck\n297\tconst OPT_IN_PREFIX = \"@tb-\";            // Pane title prefix for opt-in\n298\tconst DAEMON_URL = \"http://127.0.0.1:4000/event/normalized\";\n299\t\n300\t// State: tracked panes\n301\ttrackedPanes = Map<paneId, PaneState>;\n302\t\n303\tinterface PaneState {\n304\t  paneId: string;\n305\t  sessionId: string;           // Synthetic: tmux-%446-1719987600000\n306\t  cwd: string;\n307\t  lastOutputHash: string;\n308\t  lastOutputTime: number;\n309\t  isStuck: boolean;\n310\t  firstSeenAt: number;\n311\t}\n312\t\n313\t// Main poll loop\n314\tfunction pollLoop() {\n315\t  while (true) {\n316\t    sleep(POLL_INTERVAL_MS);\n317\t\n318\t    // 1. Discover opted-in panes\n319\t    const optedInPanes = discoverOptedInPanes();\n320\t\n321\t    // 2. Register new panes\n322\t    for (const paneId of optedInPanes) {\n323\t      if (!trackedPanes.has(paneId)) {\n324\t        registerPane(paneId);\n325\t      }\n326\t    }\n327\t\n328\t    // 3. Untrack removed panes\n329\t    for (const paneId of trackedPanes.keys()) {\n330\t      if (!optedInPanes.has(paneId)) {\n331\t        untrackPane(paneId);\n332\t      }\n333\t    }\n334\t\n335\t    // 4. Check each tracked pane\n336\t    for (const [paneId, state] of trackedPanes) {\n337\t      checkPane(paneId, state);\n338\t    }\n339\t  }\n340\t}\n341\t\n342\t// Discover opted-in panes\n343\tfunction discoverOptedInPanes(): Set<string> {\n344\t  const result = new Set<string>();\n345\t\n346\t  // List all panes with their titles\n347\t  const cmd = `tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_title}'`;\n348\t  const lines = execSync(cmd).toString().trim().split('\\n');\n349\t\n350\t  for (const line of lines) {\n351\t    const [paneId, title] = line.split(' ', 2);\n352\t    if (title.startsWith(OPT_IN_PREFIX)) {\n353\t      result.add(paneId);\n354\t    }\n355\t  }\n356\t\n357\t  return result;\n358\t}\n359\t\n360\t// Register a new pane\n361\tfunction registerPane(paneId: string) {\n362\t  const cwd = getPaneCwd(paneId);\n363\t  const sessionId = `tmux-${paneId}-${Date.now()}`;\n364\t  const output = capturePane(paneId);\n365\t  const hash = hashOutput(output);\n366\t\n367\t  trackedPanes.set(paneId, {\n368\t    paneId,\n369\t    sessionId,\n370\t    cwd,\n371\t    lastOutputHash: hash,\n372\t    lastOutputTime: Date.now(),\n373\t    isStuck: false,\n374\t    firstSeenAt: Date.now(),\n375\t  });\n376\t\n377\t  // Emit registration event\n378\t  emitEvent({\n379\t    type: \"registered\",\n380\t    sessionId,\n381\t    paneId,\n382\t    cwd,\n383\t    transcriptPath: \"\", // No transcript for synthetic sessions\n384\t    timestamp: Date.now(),\n385\t  });\n386\t\n387\t  log(`[detector] registered pane ${paneId} as ${sessionId}`);\n388\t}\n389\t\n390\t// Untrack a pane (closed or removed prefix)\n391\tfunction untrackPane(paneId: string) {\n392\t  const state = trackedPanes.get(paneId);\n393\t  if (!state) return;\n394\t\n395\t  emitEvent({\n396\t    type: \"ended\",\n397\t    sessionId: state.sessionId,\n398\t    timestamp: Date.now(),\n399\t  });\n400\t\n401\t  trackedPanes.delete(paneId);\n402\t  log(`[detector] untracked pane ${paneId}`);\n403\t}\n404\t\n405\t// Check a single pane for stuck state\n406\tfunction checkPane(paneId: string, state: PaneState) {\n407\t  const now = Date.now();\n408\t\n409\t  // 1. Verify pane still exists\n410\t  if (!paneExists(paneId)) {\n411\t    untrackPane(paneId);\n412\t    return;\n413\t  }\n414\t\n415\t  // 2. Capture output\n416\t  const output = capturePane(paneId);\n417\t  const hash = hashOutput(output);\n418\t  const outputChanged = (hash !== state.lastOutputHash);\n419\t\n420\t  // 3. Handle output change\n421\t  if (outputChanged) {\n422\t    state.lastOutputHash = hash;\n423\t    state.lastOutputTime = now;\n424\t\n425\t    // If was stuck, now unstuck\n426\t    if (state.isStuck) {\n427\t      state.isStuck = false;\n428\t      emitEvent({\n429\t        type: \"unstuck\",\n430\t        sessionId: state.sessionId,\n431\t        timestamp: now,\n432\t      });\n433\t      log(`[detector] unstuck: ${state.sessionId} (output changed)`);\n434\t    }\n435\t\n436\t    return; // Not stuck, continue monitoring\n437\t  }\n438\t\n439\t  // 4. Output hasn't changed — check quiet threshold\n440\t  const timeSinceOutput = now - state.lastOutputTime;\n441\t  const isQuiet = (timeSinceOutput >= QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS);\n442\t\n443\t  if (isQuiet && !state.isStuck) {\n444\t    // Quiet threshold exceeded — check if looks like prompt\n445\t    if (looksLikePrompt(output)) {\n446\t      // Transition to stuck\n447\t      state.isStuck = true;\n448\t      emitEvent({\n449\t        type: \"stuck\",\n450\t        sessionId: state.sessionId,\n451\t        paneId: state.paneId,\n452\t        cwd: state.cwd,\n453\t        transcriptPath: \"\",\n454\t        reason: \"stopped\", // Tmux detector can't distinguish permission vs stopped\n455\t        message: getLastLine(output),\n456\t        timestamp: now,\n457\t      });\n458\t      log(`[detector] stuck: ${state.sessionId} (quiet for ${timeSinceOutput}ms)`);\n459\t    }\n460\t  }\n461\t}\n462\t\n463\t// Capture pane output via tmux\n464\tfunction capturePane(paneId: string): string {\n465\t  const cmd = `tmux capture-pane -p -t ${paneId}`;\n466\t  return execSync(cmd, { stdio: [\"ignore\", \"pipe\", \"ignore\"] })\n467\t    .toString()\n468\t    .trim();\n469\t}\n470\t\n471\t// Hash output for comparison (avoid storing full content)\n472\tfunction hashOutput(output: string): string {\n473\t  if (!output) return \"\";\n474\t  const lines = output.split('\\n');\n475\t  const firstLine = lines[0] || \"\";\n476\t  const lastLine = lines[lines.length - 1] || \"\";\n477\t  return `${firstLine.length}-${lastLine.length}-${lines.length}-${firstLine.slice(0, 10)}-${lastLine.slice(-10)}`;\n478\t}\n479\t\n480\t// Check if last line looks like a prompt\n481\tfunction looksLikePrompt(output: string): boolean {\n482\t  const lines = output.split('\\n');\n483\t  const lastLine = lines[lines.length - 1].trim();\n484\t\n485\t  for (const pattern of PROMPT_PATTERNS) {\n486\t    if (pattern.test(lastLine)) {\n487\t      return true;\n488\t    }\n489\t  }\n490\t\n491\t  return false;\n492\t}\n493\t\n494\t// Get last line for context\n495\tfunction getLastLine(output: string): string {\n496\t  const lines = output.split('\\n');\n497\t  return lines[lines.length - 1].trim() || \"[no output]\";\n498\t}\n499\t\n500\t// Get pane cwd via tmux\n501\tfunction getPaneCwd(paneId: string): string {\n502\t  try {\n503\t    const cmd = `tmux display -p -t ${paneId} '#{pane_current_path}'`;\n504\t    return execSync(cmd, { stdio: [\"ignore\", \"pipe\", \"ignore\"] })\n505\t      .toString()\n506\t      .trim();\n507\t  } catch {\n508\t    return \"\";\n509\t  }\n510\t}\n511\t\n512\t// Emit event to daemon\n513\tasync function emitEvent(event: NormalizedEvent): Promise<boolean> {\n514\t  try {\n515\t    const response = await fetch(DAEMON_URL, {\n516\t      method: \"POST\",\n517\t      headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" },\n518\t      body: JSON.stringify(event),\n519\t    });\n520\t    return response.ok;\n521\t  } catch (err) {\n522\t    log(`[detector] emit error: ${err}`);\n523\t    return false;\n524\t  }\n525\t}\n526\t\n527\t// Prompt patterns (configurable)\n528\tconst PROMPT_PATTERNS = [\n529\t  /\\$\\s*$/,           // bash/zsh $\n530\t  />\\s*$/,            // many shells >\n531\t  /#\\s*$/,            // root #\n532\t  /\\?\\s*$/,           // confirmation prompts\n533\t  /\\[.*?\\]\\s*$/,      // bracketed prompts like [y/N]\n534\t  /:\\s*$/,            // colon prompts\n535\t  />>>\\s*$/,          // Python REPL\n536\t  /\\.\\.\\.\\s*$/,       // Python continuation\n537\t  />\\s*\\>/,           // MySQL prompt\n538\t  /@/,                // Augie/other shells\n539\t];\n540\t```\n541\t\n542\t---\n543\t\n544\t## Error Handling & Edge Cases\n545\t\n546\t### Pane closed during monitoring\n547\t\n548\t**Detection:** `pane_exists()` returns `false` on poll cycle\n549\t\n550\t**Action:** Emit `ended` event, remove from tracking\n551\t\n552\t```javascript\n553\tif (!paneExists(paneId)) {\n554\t  untrackPane(paneId);\n555\t  return;\n556\t}\n557\t```\n558\t\n559\t### Pane title loses `@tb-` prefix\n560\t\n561\t**Detection:** Pane no longer appears in `discoverOptedInPanes()`\n562\t\n563\t**Action:** Emit `ended` event, remove from tracking\n564\t\n565\t### Pane reused by new session (same pane ID, different process)\n566\t\n567\t**Detection:** Next poll cycle will see it still has `@tb-` prefix\n568\t\n569\t**Action:** Continue tracking (synthetic session ID unchanged, but that's acceptable)\n570\t\n571\t**Limitation:** If the new session is actually a different Claude Code session, the detector won't know. This is acceptable for a fallback detector.\n572\t\n573\t### Daemon not running\n574\t\n575\t**Detection:** `fetch(DAEMON_URL)` fails or returns non-200\n576\t\n577\t**Action:** Log warning, continue polling (pane state tracked locally, events lost until daemon restarts)\n578\t\n579\t```javascript\n580\tif (!response.ok) {\n581\t  log(`[detector] daemon error: ${response.status}`);\n582\t  // Continue polling — will retry on next cycle\n583\t  return false;\n584\t}\n585\t```\n586\t\n587\t### tmux command fails\n588\t\n589\t**Detection:** `execSync()` throws\n590\t\n591\t**Action:** Return empty string / false, skip pane on this cycle\n592\t\n593\t```javascript\n594\ttry {\n595\t  return execSync(cmd).toString().trim();\n596\t} catch {\n597\t  return \"\"; // Graceful degradation\n598\t}\n599\t```\n600\t\n601\t### High CPU usage from many panes\n602\t\n603\t**Mitigation:**\n604\t- Poll interval is configurable (default 2s)\n605\t- Each `capture-pane` is lightweight (text buffer copy)\n606\t- For >20 panes, consider increasing poll interval\n607\t\n608\t### Clock skew\n609\t\n610\t**Not an issue:** All timestamps are from `Date.now()` (local system time)\n611\t\n612\t---\n613\t\n614\t## Integration with Daemon\n615\t\n616\tThe detector emits events to the daemon's `/event/normalized` endpoint using the contract defined in `normalized-event-contract.md`.\n617\t\n618\t**Events emitted:**\n619\t\n620\t1. **`registered`** — When a pane with `@tb-` prefix is first discovered\n621\t2. **`stuck`** — When a quiet pane at a prompt exceeds the quiet threshold\n622\t3. **`unstuck`** — When a stuck pane produces new output\n623\t4. **`ended`** — When a pane closes or loses the `@tb-` prefix\n624\t\n625\t**Special considerations for synthetic sessions:**\n626\t\n627\t- `transcriptPath` is always `\"\"` (empty string) — synthetic sessions have no transcripts\n628\t- `reason` is always `\"stopped\"` — detector cannot distinguish `permission` vs `stopped`\n629\t- `sessionId` is synthetic (`tmux-%446-1719987600000`) — not a harness-provided ID\n630\t- `cwd` is from `pane_current_path` — tmux's best effort at the pane's working directory\n631\t\n632\t**Daemon behavior:**\n633\t\n634\tThe daemon treats synthetic sessions identically to hook-based sessions for queue purposes:\n635\t\n636\t- Stuck synthetic sessions appear in the queue\n637\t- Navigation works the same (pane ID is valid)\n638\t- `skip` and `next` work identically\n639\t\n640\t**Reconcile loop behavior:**\n641\t\n642\tSynthetic sessions have no `transcriptPath`, so the reconcile loop **cannot** verify their state by transcript tailing. It watches opted-in tmux panes and emits stuck/unstuck events to the daemon's `/event/normalized` endpoint.\n\nThis design answers the key architectural questions and provides an implementable specification.\n\n---\n\n## Design Goals\n\n1. **Harness-agnostic detection** — Works for any coding harness, not just Claude Code\n2. **Opt-in model** — Panes explicitly opt-in; no surprise monitoring\n3. **Low false-positive rate** — Avoid flagging active sessions as stuck\n4. **Self-contained operation** — No harness hooks required\n5. **Graceful degradation** — Handles panes that close, disappear, or change state\n\n---\n\n## Key Design Decisions\n\n### 1. Opt-In Mechanism\n\n**Decision: Pane-title prefix pattern**\n\nPanes opt-in by including a specific prefix in their title. The detector polls all panes and filters for those with the matching prefix.\n\n**Why not alternatives:**\n\n| Alternative | Rejected Because |\n|-------------|------------------|\n| tmux user option (`@trailboss-monitor`) | Requires pane-specific configuration per session; not discoverable via `list-panes`; doesn't persist across pane reuse |\n| Manual pane ID registration | Requires user to know pane IDs upfront; doesn't handle dynamic pane creation |\n| Environment variable in pane | Not discoverable from outside the pane; requires harness cooperation |\n| Session name pattern | Too coarse; affects all panes in a session |\n\n**Chosen approach:**\n\n- **Prefix:** `@tb-` (trail-boss)\n- **Detection:** `tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_title}' | grep '@tb-'`\n- **Example pane title:** `@tb-alpha: implementing feature X`\n- **User sets it via:** `tmux rename-window '@tb-alpha: working on task'` or shell that sets the title\n\n**Advantages:**\n- Visible to the user (they can see which panes are monitored)\n- Discoverable via standard tmux commands\n- Works across sessions and windows\n- No per-pane configuration files\n- Harness-agnostic (just a title string)\n\n**Opt-out mechanism:** User removes the prefix from the title; detector automatically stops tracking.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Detecting \"Quiet\"\n\n**Decision: `capture-pane` output hash comparison**\n\nThe detector captures the visible output of each opted-in pane on each poll cycle and computes a hash of the content. If the hash hasn't changed across polls and the quiet threshold has elapsed, the pane is considered \"quiet.\"\n\n**Why this approach:**\n\n- **Reliable:** `tmux capture-pane -p -t <pane>` returns the exact visible content\n- **No harness cooperation needed:** Works for any process running in the pane\n- **Portable:** Standard tmux command, available on all systems\n- **Deterministic:** Same content → same hash\n\n**Hash algorithm (simplified for speed):**\n\n```\nhash = concat(\n  first_line_length,\n  last_line_length,\n  first_10_chars_of_first_line,\n  last_10_chars_of_last_line,\n  total_line_count\n)\n```\n\nThis avoids storing full pane contents while detecting changes with high confidence. False positives are unlikely in practice (different content producing identical hash values).\n\n**Poll interval:** 2 seconds (configurable)\n\n- Tradeoff: Lower interval = faster detection but more CPU usage\n- 2 seconds catches stuck sessions within a few seconds of occurrence\n- tmux `capture-pane` is lightweight; overhead is acceptable\n\n---\n\n### 3. Prompt-Like Last Line Detection\n\n**Decision: Regex pattern matching on last non-empty line**\n\nBefore declaring a pane \"stuck,\" the detector checks whether the last line looks like a prompt. This reduces false positives (e.g., a long-running command with no output yet).\n\n**Prompt patterns (configurable):**\n\n```javascript\nconst PROMPT_PATTERNS = [\n  /\\$\\s*$/,           // bash/zsh $\n  />\\s*$/,            // many shells >\n  /#\\s*$/,            // root #\n  /\\?\\s*$/,           // confirmation prompts\n  /\\[.*?\\]\\s*$/,      // bracketed prompts like [y/N]\n  /:\\s*$/,            // colon prompts\n  />>>\\s*$/,          // Python REPL\n  /\\.\\.\\.\\s*$/,       // Python continuation\n  />\\s*\\>/,           // MySQL prompt\n  /@/,                // Augie/other shells\n];\n```\n\n**Algorithm:**\n\n```\n1. Capture pane output\n2. Split by newlines\n3. Find last non-empty line\n4. Trim whitespace\n5. Match against PROMPT_PATTERNS\n6. If any pattern matches → \"looks like prompt\" → can be stuck\n7. If no pattern matches → not stuck (might be mid-computation)\n```\n\n**False-positive mitigation:**\n\n- A pane that's quiet but whose last line doesn't match any prompt pattern is **not** considered stuck\n- Example: A long-running `make` with no output yet → last line might be the command itself, not a prompt → not stuck\n- Once actual output appears, the prompt detection will re-evaluate on the next quiet period\n\n**Extensibility:**\n\n- Patterns are configurable via environment variable or config file\n- Users can add harness-specific patterns (e.g., Augie's `@` prompt)\n- Future enhancement: Learn prompts from pane history\n\n---\n\n### 4. Quiet Threshold\n\n**Decision: 30 seconds (configurable)**\n\nA pane must be quiet for 30 seconds before being considered \"stuck.\"\n\n**Why 30 seconds:**\n\n- **Not too short:** Avoids flagging momentary pauses (e.g., agent thinking, network latency)\n- **Not too long:** Catches stuck sessions within a reasonable time\n- **Human scale:** 30 seconds is perceptible but not annoying\n- **Empirical:** Claude Code turns often complete within seconds; 30s suggests a genuine block\n\n**Tradeoffs:**\n\n| Threshold | Pros | Cons |\n|-----------|------|------|\n| 10s | Faster detection | More false positives (thinking periods) |\n| 30s (chosen) | Balanced | Slower to catch very short blocks |\n| 60s | Fewer false positives | Slower detection; user may notice first |\n\n**Configurability:**\n\n- Environment variable: `TRAILBOSS_QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS` (default: 30000)\n- CLI flag: `--quiet-threshold <ms>` (for detector script)\n- Config file: `~/.config/trail-boss/config.toml` (future)\n\n---\n\n### 5. Unstuck Detection\n\n**Decision: Any output change = unstuck**\n\nWhen a pane is marked as stuck, the detector continues polling. On the next poll cycle:\n\n1. Capture pane output\n2. Compute hash\n3. Compare to last-known hash\n4. If hash changed → emit `unstuck` event → clear stuck state\n\n**Why this is correct:**\n\n- **Universal:** Any new output means the session is no longer blocked\n- **Prompt-agnostic:** Works for any harness, any prompt style\n- **Covers all cases:**\n  - User typed input → new output → unstuck\n  - Agent resumed (e.g., after auto-retry) → new output → unstuck\n  - Command finished → new prompt → unstuck\n\n**Edge cases handled:**\n\n- **Pane closed:** Detected via `pane_exists()` check → emit `ended` event\n- **Pane reused by new session:** Detected via title change (if title doesn't match `@tb-` prefix) → automatically untracked\n- **Transient output (e.g., blinking cursor):** Hash comparison ignores whitespace-only changes\n\n---\n\n### 6. Session ID Generation\n\n**Decision: Synthetic session ID from pane ID + timestamp**\n\nFor the tmux detector, there is no harness-provided session ID. The detector generates a **synthetic session ID** that uniquely identifies a pane monitoring session.\n\n**Format:** `tmux-{paneId}-{startTimestamp}`\n\n**Example:** `tmux-%446-1719987600000`\n\n**Why this format:**\n\n- **Pane ID:** Ties the synthetic session to a specific tmux pane (`%446`)\n- **Start timestamp:** Makes the ID unique across restarts (same pane reused later = different ID)\n- **Prefix `tmux-`:** Clearly indicates this is a synthetic session from the detector\n\n**Stability:**\n\n- The synthetic ID is generated when the detector first starts tracking a pane\n- It persists until:\n  - The pane is closed (`ended` event)\n  - The pane title no longer matches `@tb-` (automatic untrack)\n  - The detector restarts (new synthetic IDs for all panes)\n\n**Bootstrap entries in daemon:**\n\nWhen a pane is first detected as stuck, the daemon receives a `stuck` event with a synthetic `sessionId`. The daemon treats this as a **bootstrap entry** — a session that exists only for queue purposes, with no transcript or reconcile loop.\n\n**Limitations:**\n\n- **No transcript path:** Synthetic sessions have no `transcript.jsonl` to reconcile\n- **No `cwd` auto-discovery:** Must use `pane_current_path` (tmux built-in)\n- **No harness-specific context:** Can't distinguish `permission` vs `stopped` — always uses `reason: \"stopped\"`\n- **Fragile across restarts:** Detector restart → new synthetic IDs → old entries orphaned (daemon will age them out)\n\nThese limitations are acceptable for a **fallback detector** — the primary Claude Code adapter (hooks) provides full fidelity.\n\n---\n\n## State Machine\n\nPer-pane state machine:\n\n```\n                    ┌─────────────────┐\n                    │   UNTRACKED     │  ← Pane doesn't exist or title lacks @tb- prefix\n                    └────────┬────────┘\n                             │ pane appears with @tb- title\n                             ▼\n                    ┌─────────────────┐\n                    │   REGISTERED    │  ← Initial registration, emit 'registered' event\n                    └────────┬────────┘\n                             │\n                             │ poll loop\n                             ▼\n                    ┌─────────────────┐\n          ┌────────▶│   MONITORING    │ ◀─────┐  ← Normal polling state\n          │         └────────┬────────┘      │\n          │                  │               │\n          │                  │ output        │ quiet for >30s\n          │                  │ changed       │ AND last line looks\n          │                  │               │ like prompt\n          │                  │               │\n          │    ┌─────────────┴───────────────┴────────────┐\n          │    │                                       │\n          │    │ (was stuck)                          │ (was not stuck)\n          │    ▼                                       ▼\n          │ ┌─────────┐                         ┌─────────────┐\n          │ │ UNSTUCK │                         │    STUCK    │  ← Emit 'stuck' event\n          │ └────┬────┘                         └──────┬──────┘\n          │      │                                     │\n          │      │ emit 'unstuck' event                │\n          │      └─────────────┬───────────────────────┘\n          │                    │\n          └────────────────────┘\n                                │\n                                │ pane closed or title loses @tb-\n                                ▼\n                         ┌─────────────────┐\n                         │  UNTRACKING     │  ← Emit 'ended' event\n                         └─────────────────┘\n```\n\n**States:**\n\n- **UNTRACKED:** Not monitoring (pane doesn't exist or title lacks prefix)\n- **REGISTERED:** Initial registration (emits `registered` event, transitions to MONITORING)\n- **MONITORING:** Normal polling (checking for output changes)\n- **STUCK:** Quiet for >30s at a prompt (emitted `stuck` event, awaiting output change)\n- **UNSTUCK:** Output changed after being stuck (emits `unstuck` event, returns to MONITORING)\n- **UNTRACKING:** Pane closed or prefix removed (emits `ended` event, removes from tracking)\n\n---\n\n## Poll Loop Pseudocode\n\n```javascript\n// Configuration\nconst POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 2000;           // Check every 2 seconds\nconst QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS = 30000;         // 30 seconds of quiet = stuck\nconst OPT_IN_PREFIX = \"@tb-\";            // Pane title prefix for opt-in\nconst DAEMON_URL = \"http://127.0.0.1:4000/event/normalized\";\n\n// State: tracked panes\ntrackedPanes = Map<paneId, PaneState>;\n\ninterface PaneState {\n  paneId: string;\n  sessionId: string;           // Synthetic: tmux-%446-1719987600000\n  cwd: string;\n  lastOutputHash: string;\n  lastOutputTime: number;\n  isStuck: boolean;\n  firstSeenAt: number;\n}\n\n// Main poll loop\nfunction pollLoop() {\n  while (true) {\n    sleep(POLL_INTERVAL_MS);\n\n    // 1. Discover opted-in panes\n    const optedInPanes = discoverOptedInPanes();\n\n    // 2. Register new panes\n    for (const paneId of optedInPanes) {\n      if (!trackedPanes.has(paneId)) {\n        registerPane(paneId);\n      }\n    }\n\n    // 3. Untrack removed panes\n    for (const paneId of trackedPanes.keys()) {\n      if (!optedInPanes.has(paneId)) {\n        untrackPane(paneId);\n      }\n    }\n\n    // 4. Check each tracked pane\n    for (const [paneId, state] of trackedPanes) {\n      checkPane(paneId, state);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n// Discover opted-in panes\nfunction discoverOptedInPanes(): Set<string> {\n  const result = new Set<string>();\n\n  // List all panes with their titles\n  const cmd = `tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_title}'`;\n  const lines = execSync(cmd).toString().trim().split('\\n');\n\n  for (const line of lines) {\n    const [paneId, title] = line.split(' ', 2);\n    if (title.startsWith(OPT_IN_PREFIX)) {\n      result.add(paneId);\n    }\n  }\n\n  return result;\n}\n\n// Register a new pane\nfunction registerPane(paneId: string) {\n  const cwd = getPaneCwd(paneId);\n  const sessionId = `tmux-${paneId}-${Date.now()}`;\n  const output = capturePane(paneId);\n  const hash = hashOutput(output);\n\n  trackedPanes.set(paneId, {\n    paneId,\n    sessionId,\n    cwd,\n    lastOutputHash: hash,\n    lastOutputTime: Date.now(),\n    isStuck: false,\n    firstSeenAt: Date.now(),\n  });\n\n  // Emit registration event\n  emitEvent({\n    type: \"registered\",\n    sessionId,\n    paneId,\n    cwd,\n    transcriptPath: \"\", // No transcript for synthetic sessions\n    timestamp: Date.now(),\n  });\n\n  log(`[detector] registered pane ${paneId} as ${sessionId}`);\n}\n\n// Untrack a pane (closed or removed prefix)\nfunction untrackPane(paneId: string) {\n  const state = trackedPanes.get(paneId);\n  if (!state) return;\n\n  emitEvent({\n    type: \"ended\",\n    sessionId: state.sessionId,\n    timestamp: Date.now(),\n  });\n\n  trackedPanes.delete(paneId);\n  log(`[detector] untracked pane ${paneId}`);\n}\n\n// Check a single pane for stuck state\nfunction checkPane(paneId: string, state: PaneState) {\n  const now = Date.now();\n\n  // 1. Verify pane still exists\n  if (!paneExists(paneId)) {\n    untrackPane(paneId);\n    return;\n  }\n\n  // 2. Capture output\n  const output = capturePane(paneId);\n  const hash = hashOutput(output);\n  const outputChanged = (hash !== state.lastOutputHash);\n\n  // 3. Handle output change\n  if (outputChanged) {\n    state.lastOutputHash = hash;\n    state.lastOutputTime = now;\n\n    // If was stuck, now unstuck\n    if (state.isStuck) {\n      state.isStuck = false;\n      emitEvent({\n        type: \"unstuck\",\n        sessionId: state.sessionId,\n        timestamp: now,\n      });\n      log(`[detector] unstuck: ${state.sessionId} (output changed)`);\n    }\n\n    return; // Not stuck, continue monitoring\n  }\n\n  // 4. Output hasn't changed — check quiet threshold\n  const timeSinceOutput = now - state.lastOutputTime;\n  const isQuiet = (timeSinceOutput >= QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS);\n\n  if (isQuiet && !state.isStuck) {\n    // Quiet threshold exceeded — check if looks like prompt\n    if (looksLikePrompt(output)) {\n      // Transition to stuck\n      state.isStuck = true;\n      emitEvent({\n        type: \"stuck\",\n        sessionId: state.sessionId,\n        paneId: state.paneId,\n        cwd: state.cwd,\n        transcriptPath: \"\",\n        reason: \"stopped\", // Tmux detector can't distinguish permission vs stopped\n        message: getLastLine(output),\n        timestamp: now,\n      });\n      log(`[detector] stuck: ${state.sessionId} (quiet for ${timeSinceOutput}ms)`);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n// Capture pane output via tmux\nfunction capturePane(paneId: string): string {\n  const cmd = `tmux capture-pane -p -t ${paneId}`;\n  return execSync(cmd, { stdio: [\"ignore\", \"pipe\", \"ignore\"] })\n    .toString()\n    .trim();\n}\n\n// Hash output for comparison (avoid storing full content)\nfunction hashOutput(output: string): string {\n  if (!output) return \"\";\n  const lines = output.split('\\n');\n  const firstLine = lines[0] || \"\";\n  const lastLine = lines[lines.length - 1] || \"\";\n  return `${firstLine.length}-${lastLine.length}-${lines.length}-${firstLine.slice(0, 10)}-${lastLine.slice(-10)}`;\n}\n\n// Check if last line looks like a prompt\nfunction looksLikePrompt(output: string): boolean {\n  const lines = output.split('\\n');\n  const lastLine = lines[lines.length - 1].trim();\n\n  for (const pattern of PROMPT_PATTERNS) {\n    if (pattern.test(lastLine)) {\n      return true;\n    }\n  }\n\n  return false;\n}\n\n// Get last line for context\nfunction getLastLine(output: string): string {\n  const lines = output.split('\\n');\n  return lines[lines.length - 1].trim() || \"[no output]\";\n}\n\n// Get pane cwd via tmux\nfunction getPaneCwd(paneId: string): string {\n  try {\n    const cmd = `tmux display -p -t ${paneId} '#{pane_current_path}'`;\n    return execSync(cmd, { stdio: [\"ignore\", \"pipe\", \"ignore\"] })\n      .toString()\n      .trim();\n  } catch {\n    return \"\";\n  }\n}\n\n// Emit event to daemon\nasync function emitEvent(event: NormalizedEvent): Promise<boolean> {\n  try {\n    const response = await fetch(DAEMON_URL, {\n      method: \"POST\",\n      headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" },\n      body: JSON.stringify(event),\n    });\n    return response.ok;\n  } catch (err) {\n    log(`[detector] emit error: ${err}`);\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n\n// Prompt patterns (configurable)\nconst PROMPT_PATTERNS = [\n  /\\$\\s*$/,           // bash/zsh $\n  />\\s*$/,            // many shells >\n  /#\\s*$/,            // root #\n  /\\?\\s*$/,           // confirmation prompts\n  /\\[.*?\\]\\s*$/,      // bracketed prompts like [y/N]\n  /:\\s*$/,            // colon prompts\n  />>>\\s*$/,          // Python REPL\n  /\\.\\.\\.\\s*$/,       // Python continuation\n  />\\s*\\>/,           // MySQL prompt\n  /@/,                // Augie/other shells\n];\n```\n\n---\n\n## Error Handling & Edge Cases\n\n### Pane closed during monitoring\n\n**Detection:** `pane_exists()` returns `false` on poll cycle\n\n**Action:** Emit `ended` event, remove from tracking\n\n```javascript\nif (!paneExists(paneId)) {\n  untrackPane(paneId);\n  return;\n}\n```\n\n### Pane title loses `@tb-` prefix\n\n**Detection:** Pane no longer appears in `discoverOptedInPanes()`\n\n**Action:** Emit `ended` event, remove from tracking\n\n### Pane reused by new session (same pane ID, different process)\n\n**Detection:** Next poll cycle will see it still has `@tb-` prefix\n\n**Action:** Continue tracking (synthetic session ID unchanged, but that's acceptable)\n\n**Limitation:** If the new session is actually a different Claude Code session, the detector won't know. This is acceptable for a fallback detector.\n\n### Daemon not running\n\n**Detection:** `fetch(DAEMON_URL)` fails or returns non-200\n\n**Action:** Log warning, continue polling (pane state tracked locally, events lost until daemon restarts)\n\n```javascript\nif (!response.ok) {\n  log(`[detector] daemon error: ${response.status}`);\n  // Continue polling — will retry on next cycle\n  return false;\n}\n```\n\n### tmux command fails\n\n**Detection:** `execSync()` throws\n\n**Action:** Return empty string / false, skip pane on this cycle\n\n```javascript\ntry {\n  return execSync(cmd).toString().trim();\n} catch {\n  return \"\"; // Graceful degradation\n}\n```\n\n### High CPU usage from many panes\n\n**Mitigation:**\n- Poll interval is configurable (default 2s)\n- Each `capture-pane` is lightweight (text buffer copy)\n- For >20 panes, consider increasing poll interval\n\n### Clock skew\n\n**Not an issue:** All timestamps are from `Date.now()` (local system time)\n\n---\n\n## Integration with Daemon\n\nThe detector emits events to the daemon's `/event/normalized` endpoint using the contract defined in `normalized-event-contract.md`.\n\n**Events emitted:**\n\n1. **`registered`** — When a pane with `@tb-` prefix is first discovered\n2. **`stuck`** — When a quiet pane at a prompt exceeds the quiet threshold\n3. **`unstuck`** — When a stuck pane produces new output\n4. **`ended`** — When a pane closes or loses the `@tb-` prefix\n\n**Special considerations for synthetic sessions:**\n\n- `transcriptPath` is always `\"\"` (empty string) — synthetic sessions have no transcripts\n- `reason` is always `\"stopped\"` — detector cannot distinguish `permission` vs `stopped`\n- `sessionId` is synthetic (`tmux-%446-1719987600000`) — not a harness-provided ID\n- `cwd` is from `pane_current_path` — tmux's best effort at the pane's working directory\n\n**Daemon behavior:**\n\nThe daemon treats synthetic sessions identically to hook-based sessions for queue purposes:\n\n- Stuck synthetic sessions appear in the queue\n- Navigation works the same (pane ID is valid)\n- `skip` and `next` work identically\n\n**Reconcile loop behavior:**\n\nSynthetic sessions have no `transcriptPath`, so the reconcile loop **cannot** verify their state by transcript tailing. They rely entirely on the detector's `unstuck` events for recovery.\n\n**Limitation:** If the detector crashes and restarts, old synthetic sessions are orphaned in the daemon's queue. The daemon should age out entries with no recent updates (future enhancement: TTL-based expiration).\n\n---\n\n## Testing Strategy\n\n### Unit tests\n\n1. **`discoverOptedInPanes()`**\n   - Mock `tmux list-panes` output\n   - Assert correct parsing and filtering by `@tb-` prefix\n\n2. **`hashOutput()`**\n   - Test with identical output → same hash\n   - Test with different output → different hash\n   - Test edge cases (empty output, single line)\n\n3. **`looksLikePrompt()`**\n   - Test against known prompt patterns\n   - Test non-prompts return `false`\n\n4. **State transitions**\n   - REGISTERED → MONITORING → STUCK → UNSTUCK → MONITORING\n   - REGISTERED → MONITORING → UNTRACKING (pane closed)\n\n### Integration tests\n\n1. **End-to-end with test tmux server**\n   - Create test tmux socket (`TMUX_TEST_SOCK`)\n   - Spawn test panes with `@tb-` prefix\n   - Run detector for N cycles\n   - Assert events emitted to test daemon endpoint\n\n2. **Daemon integration**\n   - Run real daemon on test port\n   - Run detector against it\n   - Verify sessions appear in `/queue` endpoint\n\n### Manual testing\n\n1. **Create a stuck session:**\n   ```bash\n   # In a tmux pane\n   tmux rename-window '@tb-test-pane'\n   # Run a command that blocks on input\n   read -p \"Press Enter to continue...\"\n   ```\n\n2. **Run the detector:**\n   ```bash\n   bun run daemon/tmux-detector.ts\n   ```\n\n3. **Verify:**\n   - Pane registered (`registered` event)\n   - After 30s, stuck (`stuck` event)\n   - Press Enter in pane\n   - Detector emits `unstuck` event\n   - Remove `@tb-` from title\n   - Detector emits `ended` event\n\n---\n\n## Future Enhancements (Out of Scope for v1)\n\n1. **Auto-discovery of Claude Code sessions**\n   - Detect `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` env var in pane\n   - Automatically add `@tb-` prefix to Claude Code panes\n   - Eliminate manual opt-in for Claude Code\n\n2. **Prompt pattern learning**\n   - Analyze pane history to detect common prompts\n   - Auto-add patterns to `PROMPT_PATTERNS`\n   - Persist learned patterns to config file\n\n3. **Adaptive quiet threshold**\n   - Start with default (30s)\n   - Adjust based on false-positive rate\n   - Per-pane thresholds (some panes are naturally quieter)\n\n4. **Transcript path inference**\n   - Guess transcript path from pane contents or CWD\n   - Enable reconcile loop for synthetic sessions\n   - Improve recovery robustness\n\n5. **TTL-based session expiration**\n   - Daemon ages out synthetic sessions with no updates\n   - Configurable TTL (default: 24 hours)\n   - Prevents orphaned entries from detector restarts\n\n---\n\n## Summary\n\nThis design specifies a complete tmux detector poller that:\n\n1. **Opts in via pane title prefix** (`@tb-`) — discoverable, visible, harness-agnostic\n2. **Detects quiet via `capture-pane` hash comparison** — reliable, no harness hooks\n3. **Validates prompts via regex patterns** — reduces false positives\n4. **Uses a 30-second quiet threshold** — balanced between speed and accuracy\n5. **Detects unstuck via output change** — universal signal\n6. **Generates synthetic session IDs** — enables queue participation without harness IDs\n7. **Emits to `/event/normalized`** — integrates cleanly with the daemon's adapter contract\n\nThe design is implementable, testable, and serves as a robust fallback for harness-agnostic stuck detection.\n","numLines":749,"startLine":1,"totalLines":749}}}

This document specifies the complete submission contract.\n6\t\n7\t## Endpoint\n8\t\n9\t**URL:** `http://127.0.0.1:4000/event/normalized`\n10\t\n11\t**Method:** `POST`\n12\t\n13\t**Content-Type:** `application/json`\n14\t\n15\t**Configuration:** The daemon URL is configurable via `TRAILBOSS_DAEMON_URL` environment variable (default: `http://127.0.0.1:4000/event/normalized`)\n16\t\n17\t## Request Format\n18\t\n19\t### HTTP Request\n20\t\n21\t```http\n22\tPOST /event/normalized HTTP/1.1\n23\tHost: 127.0.0.1:4000\n24\tContent-Type: application/json\n25\t\n26\t<event-payload-json>\n27\t```\n28\t\n29\t### Event Payloads\n30\t\n31\tThe tmux detector emits four event types, each with a specific structure:\n32\t\n33\t#### 1. | Minimum quiet time before declaring stuck |\n152\t| `TRAILBOSS_OPT_IN_PREFIX` | `@tb-` | Pane title prefix for opt-in monitoring |\n153\t| `TMUX` | (none) | Custom tmux socket path (for test This document specifies the complete submission contract.\n\n## Endpoint\n\n**URL:** `http://127.0.0.1:4000/event/normalized`\n\n**Method:** `POST`\n\n**Content-Type:** `application/json`\n\n**Configuration:** The daemon URL is configurable via `TRAILBOSS_DAEMON_URL` environment variable (default: `http://127.0.0.1:4000/event/normalized`)\n\n## Request Format\n\n### HTTP Request\n\n```http\nPOST /event/normalized HTTP/1.1\nHost: 127.0.0.1:4000\nContent-Type: application/json\n\n<event-payload-json>\n```\n\n### Event Payloads\n\nThe tmux detector emits four event types, each with a specific structure:\n\n#### 1. Registered Event (when pane with `@tb-` prefix is discovered)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"registered\",\n  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446-1735689600000\",\n  \"paneId\": \"%446\",\n  \"cwd\": \"/home/coding/trail-boss\",\n  \"transcriptPath\": \"\",\n  \"timestamp\": 1735689600000\n}\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `sessionId` is synthetic: `tmux-{paneId}-{timestamp}`\n- `transcriptPath` is always empty (tmux detector has no transcript file)\n- `cwd` is obtained via `tmux display -p -t {paneId} '#{pane_current_path}'`\n\n#### 2. Stuck Event (when pane is quiet for 30s and last line looks like a prompt)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"stuck\",\n  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446-1735689600000\",\n  \"paneId\": \"%446\",\n  \"cwd\": \"/home/coding/trail-boss\",\n  \"transcriptPath\": \"\",\n  \"reason\": \"stopped\",\n  \"message\": \"Quiet at prompt: $ \",\n  \"timestamp\": 1735689600000\n}\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `reason` is always `\"stopped\"` (tmux detector cannot distinguish permission blocks)\n- `message` is the last line of pane output (for context display)\n- Triggered when: `now - lastOutputTime >= QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS` AND `looksLikePrompt(output)`\n\n#### 3. Unstuck Event (when pane output changes after being stuck)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"unstuck\",\n  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446-1735689600000\",\n  \"timestamp\": 1735689660000\n}\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- Emitted when output hash changes while `isStuck == true`\n- Only `sessionId` and `timestamp` required\n\n#### 4. Ended Event (when pane is closed or `@tb-` prefix removed)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"ended\",\n  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446-1735689600000\",\n  \"timestamp\": 1735689660000\n}\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- Emitted during graceful shutdown or when pane no longer exists\n- Only `sessionId` and `timestamp` required\n\n## Response Format\n\n### Success Response\n\n```http\nHTTP/1.1 200 OK\nContent-Type: application/json\n\n{\n  \"ok\": true\n}\n```\n\n### Error Responses\n\n| Status | Body Example | Description |\n|--------|--------------|-------------|\n| `400 Bad Request` | `{\"error\": \"Invalid JSON\"}` | Request body is not valid JSON |\n| `400 Bad Request` | `{\"error\": \"Missing type field\"}` | Event payload missing `type` discriminator |\n| `400 Bad Request` | `{\"error\": \"Unknown event type\"}` | Invalid `type` value (not `stuck`/`unstuck`/`registered`/`ended`) |\n| `500 Internal Server Error` | `{\"error\": \"Internal server error\"}` | Server-side processing error |\n\n## Detector Behavior\n\n### Polling Cycle\n\nThe detector runs a poll loop every 2 seconds (configurable via `TRAILBOSS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`):\n\n1. **Discover opted-in panes** via `tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_title}'`\n2. **Register new panes** that have `@tb-` prefix in title\n3. **Untrack removed panes** that no longer have `@tb-` prefix\n4. **Check each tracked pane** for stuck state:\n   - Capture output via `tmux capture-pane -p -t {paneId}`\n   - Hash output for comparison\n   - Check quiet threshold (30s default)\n   - Check if last line looks like a prompt\n   - Emit `stuck` event if conditions met\n   - Emit `unstuck` event if output changes while stuck\n\n### Graceful Shutdown\n\nOn `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`, the detector:\n1. Emits `ended` event for all tracked panes\n2. Clears the pane tracking state\n3. Exits cleanly\n\n## Configuration\n\n| Environment Variable | Default | Description |\n|---------------------|---------|-------------|\n| `TRAILBOSS_DAEMON_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:4000/event/normalized` | Daemon endpoint URL |\n| `TRAILBOSS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` | `2000` | Poll cycle interval in milliseconds |\n| `TRAILBOSS_QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS` | `30000` | Minimum quiet time before declaring stuck |\n| `TRAILBOSS_OPT_IN_PREFIX` | `@tb-` | Pane title prefix for opt-in monitoring |\n| `TMUX` | (none) | Custom tmux socket path (for test isolation) |\n\n## Error Handling\n\nThe detector logs errors but continues operating:\n\n| Error Scenario | Log Message | Behavior |\n|----------------|-------------|----------|\n| Daemon not reachable | `[emit] Network error: ...` | Event lost, continues polling |\n| Invalid JSON response | `[emit] Daemon error: 400 - ...` | Event lost, continues polling |\n| tmux command fails | `[tmux] Failed to capture pane ...` | Skips pane this cycle, retries next cycle |\n| Poll cycle error | `[detector] poll error: ...` | Logs error, continues next cycle |\n\n## Integration Example\n\n### Starting the detector alongside the daemon\n\n```bash\n# Terminal 1: Start the daemon\ncd /home/coding/trail-boss\nbun run daemon/index.ts\n\n# Terminal 2: Start the tmux detector\ncd /home/coding/trail-boss\nbun run daemon/tmux-detector.ts\n```\n\n### Opt-in a tmux pane for monitoring\n\n```bash\n# In any tmux pane, set the title to opt-in\ntmux rename-window '@tb-feature-work'\n\n# Or set pane title\ntmux select-pane -T '@tb-task-name'\n```\n\n### Verify events are being submitted\n\nCheck detector logs for emission events:\n\n```\n[2024-07-02T12:34:56.789Z] [detector] registered pane %12 as tmux-%12-1719987600000 (cwd: /home/coding/project)\n[2024-07-02T12:35:26.789Z] [detector] stuck: tmux-%12-1719987600000 (quiet for 30000ms, last line: \"$ \")\n[2024-07-02T12:35:30.789Z] [detector] unstuck: tmux-%12-1719987600000 (output changed)\n[2024-07-02T12:36:00.789Z] [detector] untracked pane %12 (tmux-%12-1719987600000)\n```\n\nCheck daemon logs for received events:\n\n```\n[normalized] registered: tmux-%12-1 -> %12\n[normalized] stuck: tmux-%12-1 (stopped)\n[normalized] unstuck: tmux-%12-1\n[normalized] ended: tmux-%12-1\n```\n\n## Related Documents\n\n- `docs/notes/normalized-event-contract.md` — General normalized event API contract\n- `docs/notes/normalized-event-schema.md` — Complete event type definitions\n- `docs/notes/decisions.md` — Design rationale for normalized event endpoint\n- `daemon/types.ts` — TypeScript type definitions for events\n- `daemon/index.ts` — Daemon endpoint implementation\n- `daemon/tmux-detector.ts` — Detector implementation\n\n## Implementation Status\n\n✅ **Complete** — The tmux detector emits normalized events to `/event/normalized` as documented above. HTTP client for posting events\n- `types.go` - Event types and constants\n\n**Key features:**\n- Same detection logic as TypeScript version\n- Uses `@trailboss-monitor` pane option for opt-in (different from TypeScript version)\n- 2-second poll interval, 10-second stuck threshold\n- SHA256 content hashing for change detection\n- Graceful shutdown\n\n**Building:**\n```bash\ncd daemon/tmux-adapter\ngo build -o trailboss-tmux-detector .\n```\n\n**Opt-in mechanism (Go version):**\n```bash\ntmux set-option -p @trailboss-monitor 1\n```\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n- ✅ Code exists and is documented\n- ✅ Can detect stuck state in tmux panes\n- ✅ Submits events to daemon endpoint using normalized format\n\n## Testing\n\nThe TypeScript implementation has comprehensive acceptance tests in `test-tmux-detector.sh`:\n- Auto-discovers panes with `@tb-` prefix\n- Registers panes for tracking\n- Detects stuck state when quiet at a prompt\n- Enqueues with `reason='stopped'`\n- Detects activity and unstucks/dequeues\n\n## Normalized Event Contract\n\nThe detector emits events to `POST /event/normalized`:\n\n**StuckEvent:**\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"stuck\",\n  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446-1234567890\",\n  \"paneId\": \"%446\",\n  \"cwd\": \"/home/coding/project\",\n  \"transcriptPath\": \"\",\n  \"reason\": \"stopped\",\n  \"message\": \"$\",\n  \"timestamp\": 1234567890\n}\n```\n\n**UnstuckEvent:**\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"unstuck\",\n  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446-1234567890\",\n  \"timestamp\": 1234567900\n}\n```\n\n**SessionRegistered:**\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"registered\",\n  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446-1234567890\",\n  \"paneId\": \"%446\",\n  \"cwd\": \"/home/coding/project\",\n  \"transcriptPath\": \"\",\n  \"timestamp\": 1234567890\n}\n```\n\n**SessionEnded:**\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"ended\",\n  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446-1234567890\",\n  \"timestamp\": 1234567900\n}\n```\n\n## Related Documentation\n\n- `docs/notes/tmux-detector-design.md` -
